key_insight: TREK expands a student policy’s support with verified teacher proposals before GRPO refinement, so hard prompts become learnable instead of causing on-policy training to stall.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to improve reasoning and agent training using only verified trajectories, enabling black-box teachers or self-context without requiring access to teacher internals.
method: Identify hard prompts where the unaided student has very low pass rate.
Query a proposal source, keep the top-r proposals ranked by current student likelihood.
Apply a short forward-KL phase to absorb verified modes, then resume standard on-policy GRPO refinement.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, TREK improves Qwen3 across AIME 2024/2025, and also boosts ALFWorld and ScienceWorld success rates, with gains especially notable on harder task types and early training.
watch_item: Performance depends on obtaining verified proposal trajectories, so the approach may be constrained by proposal quality, verification cost, and how well the prompt-selection stage identifies truly hard cases.
paper_title: TREK: Distill to Explore, Reinforce to Refine
